title: NoVel IntersectorAl Long COVID TreAtmenT NEtwork
summary:
Long COVID can be accompanied by a variety of symptoms, such as severe fatigue, problems with concentration and memory, and limitations in daily life and at work. Because those affected are often cared for by different doctors and medical facilities, coordinating treatment can be difficult and lead to delays in diagnosis and treatment.

The study investigates whether a digital platform can improve care for people with Long COVID. The platform is designed to connect specialized clinics, private practice physicians, and rehabilitation clinics. It aims to help consolidate important information, better coordinate examinations and treatments, and plan the next steps in treatment in a targeted manner. This improved care is intended to promote a better quality of life and facilitate a return to work.

Individuals with potential Long COVID symptoms first screen themselves using a questionnaire to assess their risk of being affected by Long COVID. If they have sufficient symptoms suggestive of Long COVID, patients can receive information about the study from a physician and give their consent to participate. Important information about the patients’ health status is collected in a digital patient record. To this end, participants complete a total of five questionnaires over several weeks (Survey 1: upon enrollment; Survey 2: after three weeks; Survey 3: after eight to twelve weeks; Survey 4: after six months; Survey 5: after twelve months).  In addition, both patients and the treating study centers can provide medical findings and other documentation. The collected data is processed and used for case discussions by the expert panel, which take place approximately two to four weeks after Survey 3. Patients and their treating physicians will then receive a recommendation for further treatment, such as rehabilitation, an examination by a specialized physician, or a referral to a specialized facility.

interventions.name: Patients with suspected Long COVID and a sufficient symptom burden as measured by the Post-COVID Syndrome Score (PCS) are registered in a digital case management system, complete questionnaires at five time points, and can submit medical reports and other information. Each patient case is discussed

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•    Previous SARS-CoV-2 infection and symptoms attributed to SARS-CoV-2 (self-assessment)
•    Low, moderate, or high risk profile in the digital screening (PCS score ≥ 10.75)
•    The participant is capable of giving informed consent to the study, and written consent has been obtained
•    Ability to participate in the study (including use of the digital platform)
•    Sufficient knowledge of German
Exclusion criteria:
•    Being bedridden
